<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Log a startup warning when `TieringOffloadingSpec`'s secondary-tier KV can't be shared across tensor-parallel sizes, i.e. unless `canonical_layout` is on **and** the model's KV cache layers (and the parallel configuration) are certified parallelism-agnostic. This is the first follow-up listed in #62283.

Related: #62283, #55191 (core fix: direct caches keep TP in their namespace), #61822 (`canonical_layout` docs).

## Claims

- One warning per engine at startup when there is at least one secondary tier and either:
  - `canonical_layout` is off (direct layout), or
  - `canonical_layout` is on, but the layers can't all be certified as parallelism-agnostic (for example Mamba/GDN hybrids, which fall back to the opaque mapping), or PP, DCP or PCP is > 1. Today, this case starts up normally with nothing in the log saying sharing is off.
- No warning when canonical KV is portable, and none without secondary tiers.
- No behavior change: it doesn't raise, and lookups and namespaces are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py`: all hooks pass.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py`: 192 passed (macOS, CPU).
- New `test_tiering_spec_warns_when_secondary_tiers_are_topology_bound` drives the real `get_manager()` with the `example` tier, faking only the `/dev/shm` region and the primary tier, as the `create_worker` tests in that file do. It covers 5 cases (direct layout flagged agnostic, direct, canonical uncertified, canonical portable, no tiers) and asserts that exactly one warning is logged, or none. Mutation checks against it:
  - `spec.py` from `main`: 3 failed.
  - Gating only on `is_parallelism_agnostic`: the "direct layout flagged agnostic" case fails, so the test guards the case #62283 is about.
  - Gating only on `canonical_layout`: the "canonical uncertified" case fails.
  - Logging the warning twice: 3 failed.

  CI runs it in the "V1 KV Offload" step (`pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`).
- End-to-end on one L4 (Colab, base `04631c4915`): `vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 2048` with `OffloadingConnector`, `spec_name: TieringOffloadingSpec`, `cpu_bytes_to_use: 2 GiB`, `secondary_tiers: [{"type": "fs", "root_dir": "/tmp/kvfs"}]`. For each case I waited for `/health`, sent one completion, and counted warning lines. This run used the previous revision, which logged a separate message for each case. The trigger conditions are identical, and the current revision only merges the two messages into one.

| Model | `canonical_layout` | Healthy, completion OK | Topology warning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | off | yes | 1 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | `true` (`all_layers_portable=True`) | yes | 0 |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN hybrid) | `true` (`all_layers_portable=False`) | yes | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Log excerpts (previous two-message revision)</summary>

```text
# Qwen3-0.6B, canonical_layout off
(EngineCore pid=7823) INFO 10-19 22:37:09 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 1170 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)
(EngineCore pid=7823) WARNING 10-19 22:37:09 [spec.py:466] Secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration; set canonical_layout=true in kv_connector_extra_config to share it across TP sizes.

# Qwen3-0.6B, canonical_layout: true
(EngineCore pid=9036) INFO 10-19 22:37:59 [spec.py:589] Canonical KV layout enabled (all_layers_portable=True)
(EngineCore pid=9036) INFO 10-19 22:38:10 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 1170 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)

# Qwen3.5-0.8B, canonical_layout: true
(EngineCore pid=9775) INFO 10-19 22:41:54 [spec.py:589] Canonical KV layout enabled (all_layers_portable=False)
(EngineCore pid=9775) INFO 10-19 22:42:12 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 321 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)
(EngineCore pid=9775) WARNING 10-19 22:42:12 [spec.py:472] canonical_layout is set, but not every KV cache layer (or the parallel configuration) is parallelism-agnostic; secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration.
```

The current message for both warning cases:

```text
Secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration; sharing it across TP sizes needs canonical_layout=true in kv_connector_extra_config, parallelism-agnostic KV cache layers, and no PP, DCP or PCP.
```

</details>

## Details

- **Why:** without `canonical_layout`, the direct layout's bytes depend on the engine's parallel configuration. Engines with different TP sizes sharing a tier get silently wrong KV today (#62283), or always miss once #55191 lands. Nothing at startup tells the user why. With `canonical_layout` on, a model with layers that can't be certified (for example Mamba/GDN layers, which fall back to the opaque mapping) keeps TP in the namespace and never shares across TP sizes, and only an `all_layers_portable=False` info line hints at it.
- **Where:** `TieringOffloadingSpec.get_manager()`, next to the existing "Created TieringOffloadingManager" log. It runs once per engine on the scheduler side, whereas `__init__` also runs in the workers.
- **Condition:** `secondary_tiers and not (canonical_layout and is_parallelism_agnostic)`. It requires the user's `canonical_layout` flag, not just `is_parallelism_agnostic`: before #55191, that flag is True in exactly the direct-layout case that corrupts, so gating on it alone would hide the warning where it matters most. After #55191, `is_parallelism_agnostic` is False whenever `canonical_layout` is off, so the same condition stays correct. With `canonical_layout` on, the static `is_parallelism_agnostic` check decides whether the tier's namespace drops TP. It is also False for DCP > 1 or `world_size != tp_size` (PP or PCP > 1), so the message names "no PP, DCP or PCP" alongside the layer requirement.
- **Wording:** the warning says KV is "only valid for" engines with the same parallel configuration, not "only reusable by". Until #55191 lands, a cross-TP read on the V1 runner loads wrong KV instead of missing, and "only valid for" is accurate before and after #55191.
- **Known false positives:** the advice is harmless in each case. Excluding them would mean hardcoding tier names or more namespace rules in the spec.
  - Replicated MLA without `canonical_layout`: it can already be shared between engines with TP > 1, but still gets the warning.
  - The `example` tier (in-process memory) and the `kvcr` tier: they don't share KV across engines through the `FileMapper` namespace, but still get the warning.
- **Level:** `warning`, as the issue asks. Happy to switch to `info` if it's too noisy for single-topology deployments.
- **Docs:** no changes here. #61822 documents `canonical_layout` in the KV offloading usage guide.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR references #62283 or adds this check. #55191 changes the namespace gate in `offloading/config.py`, and this PR doesn't touch that file.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

 """Unit tests for native offloading specs and their factory."""
 
+import logging
 import os
 import uuid
 from typing import Any
@@ -430,6 +431,48 @@ def fake_region_ctor(**kwargs):
     assert region_calls[0]["rank"] == 1
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "secondary_tiers,canonical_layout,is_parallelism_agnostic,warns",
+    [
+        ([{"type": "example"}], False, True, True),
+        ([{"type": "example"}], False, False, True),
+        ([{"type": "example"}], True, False, True),
+        ([{"type": "example"}], True, True, False),
+        ([], False, False, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_tiering_spec_warns_when_secondary_tiers_are_topology_bound(
+    caplog_vllm,
+    monkeypatch,
+    secondary_tiers,
+    canonical_layout,
+    is_parallelism_agnostic,
+    warns,
+):
+    """Direct-layout KV warns even when it is flagged parallelism-agnostic."""
+    import vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.spec as tiering_spec_module
+
+    for name in ("SharedOffloadRegion", "CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager"):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(tiering_spec_module, name, MagicMock())
+    spec = _create_spec(
+        spec_name="TieringOffloadingSpec",
+        worker_kv_bytes_per_block=4096,
+        is_parallelism_agnostic=is_parallelism_agnostic,
+        canonical_layout=canonical_layout,
+        extra_config={"secondary_tiers": secondary_tiers},
+    )
+
+    spec.get_manager().shutdown()
+
+    warnings = [
+        record
+        for record in caplog_vllm.records
+        if record.name == tiering_spec_module.__name__
+        and record.levelno == logging.WARNING
+    ]
+    assert len(warnings) == int(warns)
+
+
